headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Copilot can write/modify repo state while ai-engineering-hub is an MCP/RAG agent with no documented isolation, creating default workspace interference and downstream error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers by default, while ai-engineering-hub is tagged MCP/RAG/agents and could plausibly consume shared workspace content. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty escalates above low. The pathway is plausible via file-based prompt injection if the pair shares a workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or workspace files, injected instructions in those files can influence Copilot outputs.
IF ai-engineering-hub consumes file or repo content as prompts, malicious text in that content can steer its behavior.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted repo text for ai-engineering-hub.
Review Copilot suggestions before applying them.
Add a prompt-injection filter for markdown, comments, and README content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file content and model prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com, but ai-engineering-hub has no data classes touched and no filesystem or network surface documented. The pairwise leakage path is therefore limited and not clearly shared; the main risk is accidental exposure if both are used on the same codebase.
conditions: IF both agents are used on the same repository, Copilot may transmit code snippets from that repo to its vendor API.
IF ai-engineering-hub is configured to ingest the same files, those contents can be re-exposed in its outputs.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in shared repo files.
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for Copilot.
Turn off or restrict Copilot on sensitive directories.
Scan open buffers before invoking either agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory data classification controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write_filesystem and modify_git_state, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent framework that may also act on repository artifacts, but its write or git capabilities are not documented. Because the overlap is plausible yet incomplete, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low. The conflict is most likely in shared repo state and editor buffers.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub writes files into the same repo that Copilot edits, concurrent changes can overwrite each other.
IF Copilot Workspace applies edits while ai-engineering-hub is generating repository artifacts, git state can diverge.
mitigations: Use one writer at a time for the repo.
Commit or stash changes before switching agents.
Keep ai-engineering-hub outputs in a separate directory.
Review diffs before applying Copilot Workspace edits.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or merge coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace proposes edits for human review, and ai-engineering-hub is an agents/RAG repository that could generate content consumed by Copilot. If Copilot treats that output as authoritative, errors can cascade into edited code or plans. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so the safer medium severity is warranted.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub produces code or instructions that Copilot ingests as repo context, Copilot may propagate those errors into suggested edits.
IF the human accepts Copilot Workspace edits without independent verification, the cascade reaches the repository.
mitigations: Require human review of every suggested edit.
Cross-check generated code against tests or linting.
Keep ai-engineering-hub outputs labeled as untrusted.
Use a second reviewer for high-impact changes.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before edit application.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source vendor service with GitHub repo OAuth context and vendor-only egress, while ai-engineering-hub is open-source and has no touched data classes or residency claims. No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern remains from vendor processing of repo context.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repository, Copilot vendor processing may create a policy mismatch.
IF the repository contains EU personal data and no DPA applies, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared repos.
Confirm a DPA and residency terms for Copilot use.
Restrict Copilot to non-regulated projects.
Document data-handling rules for both agents.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
